evidence: Cic. N.D. 3.69: vīnum aegrōtīs prōdest rārō, nocet saepissimē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The classical form of the adverb; rārē is ante-classical and post-Augustan, rārenter old (Lewis & Short). Rārō umquam is “hardly ever” (Quint.).

phrases.latin: ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam, saepe ante, tardius rārō
phrases.english: I wake when I like, usually about the first hour, often before, rarely later

phrases.latin: quod rārō cursōribus ēvenit, hieran fēcimus
phrases.english: as rarely happens with runners, we finished level

phrases.latin: vīnum aegrōtīs prōdest rārō, nocet saepissimē
phrases.english: wine rarely does the sick good, and very often harms them
